subject.title: [Bug]: Discord routing / mention-gating issue in OpenClaw

question: Should Discord preflight adopt strict active-target scoping by default when another configured agent, role target, quoted/later mention signal, or bot-authored message means the current agent is not being addressed?
rationale: The source gap is concrete, but the requested fix changes stable Discord routing precedence, role semantics, and bot-loop behavior for existing multi-agent guild setups.

options.title: Adopt strict active-target scoping
options.body: Implement Discord-owned target resolution before default routing, drop messages that target other configured agents, scope mention text to the opening attention window, and require live Discord proof.

options.title: Split into narrower trackers
options.body: Keep this issue as broad coordination while https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/13487, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/7717, and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/80235 own separate slices.

options.title: Document current default-owner behavior
options.body: Treat current default routing plus opt-in ignoreOtherMentions and allowBots policies as the intended contract and close or narrow conflicting requests.

recommendation.title: Adopt strict active-target scoping
recommendation.body: Implement Discord-owned target resolution before default routing, drop messages that target other configured agents, scope mention text to the opening attention window, and require live Discord proof.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest combined signal from Discord routing, mention-gating, and prior maintainer-side analysis for this behavior contract.
